headline.purpose: The app name on the first start.

headline-small.purpose: Header titles; dialog titles by Material default.

title.purpose: Names on the seated cart, sheet and pause-panel bands; Resume; achievement points; a score's rank stamp.

title-small.purpose: Names on grid carts' bands; achievement and leaderboard names on the pop-up and in the lists; ranks in a score table; Continue at 17sp.

body.purpose: Rows, menu lines, explanations; names and scores in a score table.

body-small.purpose: Summaries, help notes, times; the line under a board's name on its pop-up card.

tag.purpose: Short sentence-case tags: Empty, a choice row's label, key-table heads, the speed pill, the achievement progress count, leaderboard counters, pts, rank, list progress, a score table's gap.

shadows.name: moulded-highlight
shadows.purpose: Compose: the highlight colour fills the shape and the body is drawn 1dp lower, leaving a 1dp lit top edge.

shadows.name: moulded-shade
shadows.purpose: Compose: the shape drawn 1.5dp lower in the shade colour, a solid lip under raised plastic. Not a blurred drop shadow.

shadows.name: recessed
shadows.purpose: The slot bay: black rim along the top, faint highlight along the bottom.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Behind menus over the paused game, and under overlay pills (speed, achievement challenges and progress, leaderboard counters).

motion.name: insert
motion.purpose: The signature insert: the seated cart slides up 64dp into the slot's mouth (grid cart: up 14dp, scale 0.96), its label darkening to 60% black, then the game opens. Reset 400ms after.

motion.name: menu-appear
motion.value: 150ms default tween; alpha 0 to 1, scale 0.96 to 1
motion.purpose: The pause panel and its pages over the game.

motion.name: achievement-popup
motion.value: enter 220ms slide from -50% height + 160ms fade; exit 200ms slide to -33% + 200ms fade
motion.purpose: The achievement pop-up cart dropping in from the top of the game and leaving upward; it takes no touches.

motion.name: popup-hold
motion.value: board notes 2s; notes 3s; unlock and rank card 4s; mastered 6s
motion.purpose: How long each pop-up card shows. A board's newer card (rank, failed) takes its older card's place (sending, started), at once if that one is showing.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: With Android's Remove animations on, every animation is a cut.

breakpoints.name: pause-two-column
breakpoints.value: wider than tall and under 520dp tall

narrative.overview:
The app is the player's shelf of cartridges. Every screen is moulded cartridge plastic: light grey ABS by day and smoked black by night, switching with the phone's dark mode. Cards are not floating Material sheets but raised carts standing on that plastic, each with a narrower lip along its top edge, a 1 dp moulded highlight on top, a short shade below and fine grip ridges near the bottom. Each game's label is its own picture (box art or the frame where the player left off) under a black label band that names the game in white heavy italic. The game last played sits seated in a dark recessed slot at the top of the list, and pressing Continue slides it up into the slot's mouth before the game opens.

This is an Operate-mode app. Navigation, sheets, dialogs, switches and segmented choices are standard Material 3 components with themed colours, and the world comes through in palette, lettering, shape and one signature motion. The density is calm and physical: a few large objects per screen, generous gutters, nothing tinted for decoration. Colour comes from the game art and from one see-through-plastic accent that follows the chosen console skin. It refuses the category default of a charcoal launcher with a cover grid and a single neon accent, and it never prints Nintendo's marks.

The chrome frames the game picture and never competes with it. Over a paused game, the menu is a cartridge panel on a dark scrim, headed by that game's label band.
keyCharacteristics: Two plastics, one structure: grey by day, smoked by night, the same roles in both; the slot and label bands stay dark in both.
Games are cartridges; their labels are their pictures; names sit on black bands in white Roboto Black Italic.
One accent, derived from the console skin's plastic, marks only what can be pressed.
Label stock (pale print) is the same in both themes and appears only where something is actually printed.
Depth comes from moulding (highlight and shade lines) and recessing, not drop shadows.
The phone's own fonts only: Roboto, its Black Italic, and Roboto Condensed.

rules.name: The Pressable Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent marks only what can be pressed or what is switched on: filled buttons, the chosen segment, an on switch, a chosen ring, focus. Never a heading, a divider, an icon at rest or a decorative fill.

rules.name: The Label Red Rule
rules.body: Red means danger and errors. It is never a second accent, and danger actions sit apart from the safe ones (after a divider in sheets, last in the pause menu).

rules.name: The Printed Stock Rule
rules.body: Label stock appears only where something is printed: a box, a picture, a blank label, a filled save slot, a downloaded badge, and the user's own rank in a score table (a small printed sticker in day ink). An empty save slot, a badge not yet downloaded and a leaderboard's mark are bare plastic (cart-high), so those pages stay dark at night.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text pairing and every derived accent is at least 4.5:1, enforced by the palette and accent tests; a new colour is checked against the darkest light ground (grey plastic) and the lightest dark ground (cart-smoked-high).

rules.name: The Label Lettering Rule
rules.body: Roboto Black Italic is for names and numbers that would be printed on a cartridge: screen titles, game names on bands, slot numbers, achievement and leaderboard names, points and ranks, the Continue and Resume labels. Running text, settings and messages (a server problem, a score that couldn't be sent, a note) stay in upright Roboto; so do players' names and scores in a score table.

rules.name: The Tabular Times Rule
rules.body: Times, dates, counts, scores, ranks and slot numbers use tabular figures (tnum) so they line up and a running counter doesn't jitter; times on carts and scores in a table sit right-aligned or in the grip strip.

rules.name: The Moulded Not Floating Rule
rules.body: Raised pieces show depth only through their 1dp highlight and 1.5dp shade lines in the plastic's own colours. No blurred drop shadows, gradients or glass.

rules.name: The Dark Slot Rule
rules.body: The slot is recessed and dark in both themes; it is where a cartridge goes in, never a generic card.

dos: Do derive every accent from the chosen skin's seed through the lightness loops, and check the result against the 4.5:1 floor in both themes.
Do put a game's name on a black label band in white Roboto Black Italic wherever the game itself is the subject (carts, the game sheet, the pause panel).
Do build new raised containers from the cart colour with the moulded highlight and shade, and new recessed areas with the slot's recess.
Do keep label stock and its day inks identical in both themes, and print it only where something is printed.
Do use standard Material 3 components with the themed colours, pill buttons and the app's shapes.
Do use tabular figures for times, dates, counts, scores and ranks.
Do show a feature that is off for a reason by fading its row to 38% in place and saying why under it, rather than hiding it.
donts: Don't use the accent on anything that cannot be pressed or switched on.
Don't use label red for anything except danger and errors.
Don't add blurred drop shadows, gradients or glass; depth is moulding and recessing only.
Don't bundle or download a font; use the phone's Roboto, Roboto Black Italic and Roboto Condensed.
Don't print Nintendo's logos, the "GAME BOY ADVANCE" logotype or the seal, on screens or in the icon.
Don't make the slot light in the light theme, or put an empty save slot on label stock.
Don't use Roboto Black Italic for running text, help notes or settings rows.
